evidence_quotes.quote: qual a influência da capacidade institucional nos indicadores de acesso ao saneamento básico em Minas Gerais?

Para isso, foram consideradas dez variáveis referentes às questões financeiras, presença de corpo técnico da prefeitura atuando no setor de saneamento, o número de veículos e funcionários atuantes e a existência de plano e política de saneamento no município.

Com o auxílio de uma Análise Fatorial Exploratória, essas variáveis foram reduzidas a quatro indicadores de capacidade institucional: política, financeira, técnica e operacional, utilizadas como variáveis explicativas para a execução da regressão linear múltipla.

Como variável dependente, optou-se pela utilização dos dados acerca do atendimento/cobertura de três dos quatro serviços de saneamento básico, a saber: abastecimento de água, esgotamento sanitário e coleta de resíduos sólidos.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines municipal-level population access/coverage for water supply (Atend_Agua) and sanitary sewage (Atend_Esgoto), alongside solid waste collection (Atend_RDO), across municipalities in Minas Gerais, Brazil.
criterion_notes.c2: PASSES PLAIN WORDING / FAILS NARROW 2026-10-13 READING. Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2 ('Examines a legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory or governance factor'), this study qualifies (plain=yes -> plain_criterion2_decision='include') because it examines municipal institutional capacity across financial, technical, operational, and political/planning dimensions, including binary indicators for whether a municipality has adopted a Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan (PMSB) and Municipal Basic Sanitation Policy (PPSB) pursuant to Law 11.445/2007. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading, however, it fails (narrow=no -> decision='exclude', E03): the exposures are aggregate municipal state/resource and planning capacities (per capita operating revenues and expenditures, presence of municipal technical staff, waste workers and vehicles per 10,000 inhabitants, and general existence of a municipal sanitation plan/policy grouped via factor analysis into Capacidade Financeira, Técnica, Operacional, and Política). The paper does not examine a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access—such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff or cost-recovery rules, discretion or accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership or regulatory structure directly governing service access.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains quantitative cross-sectional empirical evidence using 2017 IBGE and 2018 SNIS municipal data across Minas Gerais, analyzed via exploratory data analysis, chi-square/ANOVA tests, exploratory factor analysis (PCA with varimax rotation), and multiple linear regression with White robust standard errors.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipal service access/coverage outcomes: total water supply coverage index (Atend_Agua, %), total sewage coverage index (Atend_Esgoto, %), and regular household solid waste collection coverage rate (Atend_RDO, %).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and unit of analysis (municipalities in Minas Gerais, Brazil; n = 574 after outlier removal in descriptive statistics, n = 391 in multiple regressions), exposures (four factor scores of municipal institutional capacity: financial, technical, operational, political), outcomes (municipal percentage coverage of water supply, sanitary sewage, and solid waste collection), and study design (cross-sectional observational econometric study) are clearly identified.
criterion_notes.c6: Published in Portuguese (with English and Portuguese abstracts), which is eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

study_design: Cross-sectional quantitative observational study (exploratory factor analysis via principal components with varimax rotation followed by OLS multiple linear regression with White robust standard errors).
population_and_sample: Municipalities of the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil (unit of analysis: municipality; n = 574 municipalities after outlier removal in exploratory/descriptive analysis; n = 391 municipalities with complete data in the final multiple linear regression models).
exposure: Municipal institutional capacity factor scores derived from 10 variables: Financial Capacity (direct and indirect operating revenue per capita, total water/sewage expenditure per capita, own-staff expenditure per capita), Technical Capacity (presence of municipal technical staff in water supply and in sanitary sewage), Operational Capacity (public cleaning/household waste employees and vehicles per 10,000 inhabitants), and Political Capacity (binary existence of a Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan [PMSB] and Municipal Public Policy of Basic Sanitation [PPSB] under Law 11.445/2007).
outcome: Municipal coverage percentages in 2018 from SNIS: total water supply attendance index (Atend_Agua, %), total sewage attendance index (Atend_Esgoto, %), and regular household solid waste collection coverage rate (Atend_RDO, %).
rationale: Full-text Portuguese empirical article matching the record metadata. The study uses 2017 IBGE and 2018 SNIS municipal data for Minas Gerais to test how four dimensions of municipal institutional capacity (financial, technical, operational, and political/planning capacity) relate to municipal coverage rates of water supply, sanitary sewage, and solid waste collection. While it satisfies Criteria 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6—and would be included under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2—it is excluded as E03 (Wrong exposure) under the 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type scope of Criterion 2 because its exposures capture general municipal state, fiscal, staffing, operational, and high-level planning capacities (including binary existence of a municipal sanitation plan/policy) rather than a specific legal, regulatory, or administrative rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility rules, tenure/documentation requirements, administrative burden, tariff/cost-recovery rules, discretion, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure directly governing access).
